title: Aivu, a Babylonian in Rav Nachman’s Time
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Bava Metzia 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.93b.12), Aivu deposits flax at Bei Dunya. Shabbu—the thief’s name—takes it, and the case comes before Rav Nachman. In [Avodah Zarah 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.35b.20), Aivu eats gentile bread; Rava, or according to another version Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, issues a rebuke that Hyman takes to mean “Do not transmit a teaching in Aivu’s name.” Hyman infers that he was a rabbinic scholar.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman glosses the rebuke as not transmitting teachings in Aivu’s name. It is not an instruction merely to stop conversing with him. The scholarly-status conclusion belongs to Hyman.

The consulted Bava Metzia 93b reads Bei Runya, rather than the supplied Bei Dunya. Avodah Zarah 35b says not to converse with Aivu; Hyman interprets the rebuke as not transmitting teachings in his name. The interpretation and the inference about his scholarship remain Hyman’s.

The [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=389&lang=en) records both episodes and gives Bei Runya for the flax deposit. The linked Avodah Zarah text says “Do not converse with Aivu.” The restriction on transmitting teachings is Hyman’s interpretation.
